title: A Bridegroom for Miss Mole
originalTitle: 두더지 사위 삼기 · Dudeoji sawi samgi
place: Near the stone Miryek by the Kingin River
note: A new adaptation of “A Bridegroom for Miss Mole,” retaining its chain of Sky, Sun, Cloud, Wind, Stone, and Mole while shortening the courtship frame.

rights.basis: Source edition published in 1922 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A small mole looks up at the sun, cloud, wind, and a great stone figure.
scenes: Father Mole adored his daughter and vowed that she would marry the mightiest being in the universe.
The wise moles named the great blue Sky, so Father Mole climbed up to make his request.
But Sky said, “Sun is mightier, for only when Sun rises can my colors be seen.” Sun replied, “Cloud can cover me completely.”
Cloud rumbled, then admitted, “Wind drives me wherever it pleases.” Wind sighed, “The great stone Miryek does not move, however hard I blow.”
Miryek listened patiently. “I withstand sky, sun, cloud, and wind,” said the stone. “Yet Mole tunnels beneath my feet. One day his burrows could topple me.”
After traveling around the world, Father Mole found the answer close to home. His daughter married a kind young mole.
Their underground wedding was joyful—and Miss Mole was pleased that someone had finally asked what suited her.
